Let $F$ be a field and let $V,W$ be $F$-vector spaces ([[def-vector-space]]). For $k\ge0$, a map

$$f:V^k\longrightarrow W$$

is **$k$-linear** (multilinear) when it is linear in each of its $k$ arguments separately, with the other arguments held fixed. It is **alternating** when

$$f(v_1,\ldots,v_k)=0\qquad\text{whenever }v_i=v_j\text{ for some }1\le i<j\le k.$$

Let $(D,\varphi)$ be a $C^2$ patch over a finite elementary Green region ([[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]]), with positive boundary chain $\partial D=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m)$ and induced boundary chain $\varphi(\partial D)$, and let $F$ be a $C^1$ vector field on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ containing $\varphi[D]$. Then the circulation around the induced boundary chain equals the flux of the curl in the induced orientation:

$$\oint_{\varphi(\partial D)}F\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_D\bigl\langle(\operatorname{curl}F)\circ\varphi,\ \varphi_u\times\varphi_v\bigr\rangle.$$

The right-hand side is the flux of $\operatorname{curl}F$ through the patch in the orientation induced by $\varphi$, in the sense of [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].
premise_quotes: **Given:** The unit square $D=[0,1]^2$; an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$; a function $a\in C^2(I)$ with $a>0$; the maps $r$, $B$, $v$ displayed in the Example; and a fixed time $t\in I$.

1.1 Setting and regularity. The map $r(u,v,t)=(a(t)u,a(t)v,0)$ is of class $C^2$ on the open set $\mathbb R^2\times I$, since it is polynomial in $(u,v)$ with $C^2$ coefficients, with $r_u=(a,0,0)$, $r_v=(0,a,0)$ and $r_u\times r_v=(0,0,a^2)\ne0$ on $D^\circ\times I$ because $a>0$; further $v(x,t)=\frac{a'(t)}{a(t)}(x_1,x_2,0)$ is $C^1$ jointly, and $v(r(u,v,t),t)=\frac{a'}{a}(au,av,0)=(a'u,a'v,0)=r_t(u,v,t)$, while $\operatorname{div}B=0$ for the constant field $B=e_3$. Thus the geometric and analytic hypotheses of [L1] hold, and $D$ is the elementary Green region of [L2]. At each time $D$ has connected interior and $r(\cdot,t)$ is injective since $a(t)>0$, so it is a regular patch for the Stokes application [L5]. [given, L1, L2, L4, algebra]

2.2 The two terms on the right-hand side. Since $B$ is constant, $\partial_tB\equiv0$ and the surface integral $\int_{S(t)}\partial_tB\cdot n\,dS$ vanishes. For the boundary term, [L4] gives $v\times B=\frac{a'}{a}(x_1,x_2,0)\times(0,0,1)=\frac{a'}{a}(x_2,-x_1,0)$ and then $\operatorname{curl}(v\times B)=\bigl(0,0,\partial_1(-\tfrac{a'}{a}x_1)-\partial_2(\tfrac{a'}{a}x_2)\bigr)=(0,0,-2\tfrac{a'}{a})=-2\tfrac{a'}{a}e_3$ at time $t$; consequently $(\operatorname{curl}(v\times B))\circ r=-2\tfrac{a'}{a}e_3$ is constant on $D$, and patch Stokes [L5] together with the constant-integral fact [L3] gives $\oint_{\partial S(t)}(v\times B)\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_D\langle-2\tfrac{a'}{a}e_3,(0,0,a^2)\rangle\,du\,dv=-2\tfrac{a'}{a}a^2\int_Ddu\,dv=-2a(t)a'(t)$. [step 1.1, L3, L4, L5, algebra]

review.evidence: The current local Stokes proof restricts phi to the inverse image of the open field domain, obtains C1 pullbacks by product/chain rules and mixed-partial cancellation, applies Green to the supplied finite elementary decomposition, then pulls back each piecewise-C1 boundary arc. C1 F supplies continuous curl; the exact flux definition requires continuity only, so the false extra C1 adjective in step 5.1 is unused. Type-I/II FTC identities and finite shared-arc cancellation establish Green; the antisymmetric derivative expansion establishes the curl identity. No derivative of curl is used. The example supplies a>0, one-piece square D, injective C2 r with nonzero area vector, and fixed-time spatially linear G=(aprime/a)(x2,-x1,0) with constant curl -2(aprime/a)e3. All regular-patch and field premises hold, including contracting/stationary cases.

Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be open, let $\varphi:O\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$, let $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\sigma_2):[a,b]\to O$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ path, and let $F$ be a continuous vector field on a set containing $\varphi(\sigma([a,b]))$. Put $P^{*}=\langle F\circ\varphi,\varphi_u\rangle$ and $Q^{*}=\langle F\circ\varphi,\varphi_v\rangle$ where these are defined. Then $\varphi\circ\sigma$ is a piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\mathbb R^3$ and the vector line integral of the field along the image arc equals the parameter line integral of the pulled-back pair:

$$\int_{\varphi\circ\sigma}F\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_{\sigma}(P^{*},Q^{*})\cdot d\mathbf r.$$
premise_quotes: [F1] Moving patch: the flux is the integral displayed in the Statement over the compact Jordan measurable region $D$; the velocity field is $C^1$ on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the swept graph and satisfies $v(r(p,t),t)=r_t(p,t)$; $r$ extends $C^2$ to a neighbourhood of $D\times I$ ([[def-em-moving-patch]]).

[F7] Parametric Stokes prerequisites, with no rank or injectivity hypothesis: [[lem-the-stokes-integrand-identity-on-a-c2-patch]] gives $\partial_uQ^*-\partial_vP^*=\langle\operatorname{curl}G\circ\varphi,\varphi_u\times\varphi_v\rangle$ for $P^*=\langle G\circ\varphi,\varphi_u\rangle$, $Q^*=\langle G\circ\varphi,\varphi_v\rangle$ on an open parameter neighbourhood. [[thm-greens-theorem-for-finite-unions-of-elementary-regions]] integrates this over any supplied finite elementary Green region, and [[lem-a-vector-line-integral-pulls-back-to-the-parameter-region]] identifies each resulting boundary arc integral with its image line integral.

4.1 Parametric Stokes and conclusion. Fix a time $t$ of the nondegenerate $I$. The spatial slices of $v,B$ are $C^1$ on the open slice of $W\cap V$ containing $r(D,t)$; hence $G=(v\times B)(\cdot,t)$ is $C^1$ there. Restrict the $C^2$ extension of $\varphi=r(\cdot,t)$ to an open neighbourhood $O\supseteq D$ mapping into that slice. The first supplier in [F7] makes $P^*,Q^*$ $C^1$ on $O$ with the displayed curl integrand. Green then gives its integral over $D$ as the positive boundary integral, and the pullback supplier identifies each arc integral with $\int_{\varphi\circ\sigma_\ell}G\cdot d\mathbf r$. Thus $\int_D\langle\operatorname{curl}(v\times B)(r,t),w\rangle\,dp=\oint_{\partial S(t)}(v\times B)\cdot d\mathbf r$ without requiring a published regular patch. Substituting into steps 2.1 and 3.1 gives the always-defined parameter identity $\Phi'(t)=\int_D\langle\partial_tB(r,t)+v(r,t)\operatorname{div}B(r,t),w\rangle\,dp-\oint_{\partial S(t)}(v\times B)\cdot d\mathbf r$. At a rank-two slice its first two integrals are exactly the surface shorthand defined in the Statement (and, for an ordinary regular patch, [F8]); if $\operatorname{div}B=0$ the middle term vanishes. This proves the stated identity with the minus sign, including relative endpoint derivatives whenever the normal shorthand applies. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F7, F8, algebra] ∎

premise_quotes:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of the
imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region
of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let
$E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the
volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the
fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional
derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$
jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

[F2] Volume test geometries are nonempty bounded open $V$ with $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ and a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentation with outward normal $\nu_V$ and the face-sum closed-surface flux; the open interior of every closed axis-parallel box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subseteq\Omega$ with $a_i<b_i$ is a volume test geometry with $\overline V=K$, and $\int_Vh\,d\lambda_3=\int_Kh\,d\lambda_3$ for continuous $h$ on a neighbourhood of $K$ because the six faces are $\lambda_3$-null. Patch test geometries are regular $C^2$ patches over finite elementary Green regions with induced boundary chain, circulation and induced orientation, and every affine patch $r(u,v)=p+ue_j+ve_k$ over an axis-parallel square whose image lies in $\Omega$ is a patch test geometry with $r_u\times r_v=e_j\times e_k$ ([[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]).

[F5] For a $C^2$ patch $(D,\varphi)$ over a finite elementary Green region and a $C^1$ vector field $F$ on an open set containing $\varphi[D]$, $\oint_{\varphi(\partial D)}F\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_D\langle(\operatorname{curl}F)\circ\varphi,\varphi_u\times\varphi_v\rangle$, the induced orientation being that of the patch ([[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]]).
